Name: Scientific Naturalism
Description: Worldview holding that natural laws govern all phenomena, the universe is self-contained, and scientific method is the primary path to knowledge.
CreationMyth: Approximately 13.8 billion years ago, the universe began in the Big Bang, an expansion from an infinitely dense singularity. Fundamental forces separated, particles formed, and after 380,000 years, atoms emerged. Gravity pulled matter into stars and galaxies. Heavy elements were forged in stellar cores and scattered by supernovae. 4.6 billion years ago, our solar system condensed from a molecular cloud. Earth formed through accretion and was bombarded by asteroids and comets that brought water. Around 3.8 billion years ago, self-replicating molecules emerged in Earth's primordial oceans. Through natural selection over billions of years, life evolved from single cells to complex multicellular organisms. Homo sapiens emerged in Africa around 300,000 years ago, developing culture, language, and eventually science to understand the cosmos.
CorePrinciples: Universe operates by natural laws, no supernatural intervention
Scientific method: observation, hypothesis, testing, revision
Evolution by natural selection explains life's diversity
Materialism: only physical matter and energy exist
Skepticism and evidence-based reasoning
Universe is indifferent to human concerns
Knowledge is provisional and subject to revision

Name: Transhumanism
Description: Intellectual movement advocating for using technology to enhance human physical and cognitive capabilities beyond current biological limitations.
CorePrinciples: Technology can and should enhance human capabilities
Death and suffering are problems to be solved, not accepted
Morphological freedom: right to modify one's body/mind
Technological singularity may radically transform existence
Intelligence explosion through AI possible
Life extension and immortality as goals
Rational scientific approach to human enhancement

Name: Deep Ecology
Description: Environmental philosophy emphasizing intrinsic value of all living beings and fundamental restructuring of human relationship with nature.
CorePrinciples: All life has intrinsic value independent of utility to humans
Ecological diversity and richness have value in themselves
Humans have no right to reduce biodiversity except to meet vital needs
Current human interference with nature is excessive
Fundamental change in economic, technological, and ideological structures needed
Self-realization through identification with all life
Ecocentric rather than anthropocentric worldview

Name: Effective Altruism
Description: Philosophical and social movement using evidence and reason to determine the most effective ways to benefit others and acting on that basis.
Sources: The Life You Can Save (Peter Singer)
CorePrinciples: Use evidence and reason to find the most effective ways to help others
Prioritize interventions by cost-effectiveness and scale
Equal moral consideration for all sentient beings
Earning to give: maximize income to donate effectively
Longtermism: consider impacts on future generations
Existential risk reduction as priority
Quantitative analysis of charitable impact

Name: Stoic Naturalism (Modern)
Description: Contemporary revival of Stoic philosophy integrated with scientific naturalism, emphasizing virtue, acceptance of nature, and rational living.
Sources: A Guide to the Good Life (William Irvine)
How to Be a Stoic (Massimo Pigliucci)
CorePrinciples: Focus on what's in your control, accept what isn't
Live according to nature and reason
Four cardinal virtues: wisdom, courage, justice, temperance
Negative visualization: contemplate loss to appreciate what you have
Dichotomy of control: distinguish internal from external
Amor fati: love of fate, embrace what happens
Cosmopolitanism: all humans are part of single community

Name: Integral Theory
Description: Comprehensive framework attempting to integrate insights from multiple disciplines and worldviews using developmental and systems perspectives.
CorePrinciples: AQAL framework: All Quadrants, All Levels, All Lines, All States, All Types
Developmental stages of consciousness
Integration of pre-modern, modern, and postmodern insights
Four quadrants: interior/exterior, individual/collective
Holarchy: nested hierarchies of increasing wholeness
Include and transcend: higher stages integrate lower ones
Multiple intelligences and developmental lines

Name: Postmodern Relativism
Description: Worldview holding that truth, morality, and meaning are culturally constructed, context-dependent, and not objectively determined; all perspectives deserve equal consideration.
Sources: The Social Construction of Reality (Berger and Luckmann)
CorePrinciples: No absolute truths; all knowledge is perspective-dependent
Culture shapes what counts as real, true, or good
All grand narratives are suspect and should be questioned
Tolerance of diversity: no culture's values are universally valid
Power structures define what gets called 'truth'
Scientific knowledge is one narrative among many
Identity and meaning are constructed, not discovered

Name: New Age Spirituality
Description: Eclectic spiritual movement drawing from diverse traditions, emphasizing personal transformation, holistic health, spiritual self-development, and the dawning of a new era of human consciousness.
CorePrinciples: All is one: the universe is fundamentally unified consciousness
Personal spiritual experience is primary over institutional religion
Spiritual evolution: humanity is evolving to higher consciousness
Law of Attraction: thoughts shape reality
Holistic health: body, mind, spirit are inseparable
Syncretic spirituality: drawing from multiple traditions
Intuition and direct experience over doctrine or dogma
Earth as living being (Gaia consciousness)

Name: Rationalism and Skeptical Inquiry
Description: Worldview applying scientific reasoning, critical thinking, and evidence-based inquiry to all claims, with organized skepticism actively examining paranormal, pseudoscientific, and supernatural claims.
Sources: How to Think Straight About Psychology (Keith Stanovich)
CorePrinciples: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence
Scientific method as the best tool for determining truth
Cognitive biases systematically distort thinking; must be actively countered
Peer review and replication as foundations of reliable knowledge
Naturalistic explanations preferred over supernatural ones
Pseudoscience and paranormal claims don't meet evidence standards
Open-minded but skeptical examination of all claims

Name: Cosmopolitanism
Description: Worldview holding that all human beings belong to a single moral community, and that global justice, rights, and responsibilities transcend national borders.
CorePrinciples: All humans have equal moral worth regardless of nationality
Global justice: obligations extend to all people, not just co-citizens
Cultural diversity is valuable but not morally decisive
International institutions and laws necessary for global order
Rights are universal, not merely cultural conventions
Shared global challenges (climate, pandemics) require global solutions
Identity is layered and multiple, not fixed to one community
NotableFigures: Diogenes of Sinope (coined 'citizen of the world')

Name: Minimalism and Voluntary Simplicity
Description: Lifestyle and philosophical movement rejecting excessive consumption and materialism in favor of intentional simplicity, focusing on what genuinely contributes to wellbeing.
Sources: Your Money or Your Life (Vicki Robin)
The Minimalists (Joshua Fields Millburn and Ryan Nicodemus)
CorePrinciples: Owning fewer possessions creates greater freedom and happiness
Consumption does not equal meaning or identity
Intentional living: deliberately choosing what to keep
Financial independence through reduced spending
Environmental benefit: consuming less reduces ecological impact
Time and attention are more valuable than things
Quality over quantity in relationships, possessions, and commitments

Name: Accelerationism
Description: Diverse political-philosophical tendency arguing that the contradictions of capitalism or technology should be accelerated rather than resisted, to force rapid transformation of society.
Sources: Inventing the Future (Srnicek and Williams — Left Accelerationism)
CorePrinciples: Technology and capitalism's internal dynamics should be accelerated, not slowed
Left Accelerationism (L/ACC): harness technology for post-scarcity and liberation
Universal basic income, automation, and reduced work as goals
Rejection of folk politics and localism as too slow for global problems
Right Accelerationism: civilization's collapse will produce stronger order
E/ACC (Effective Accelerationism): AI and technological growth are net positive unconditionally
Futures must be actively constructed, not just reacted to
NotableFigures: Nick Srnicek and Alex Williams (left variant)

Name: Perennial Philosophy
Description: Philosophical and spiritual perspective arguing that all major world religions and wisdom traditions share a common core of universal truths about the nature of consciousness, reality, and the divine.
Sources: The Transcendent Unity of Religions (Frithjof Schuon)
CorePrinciples: All religions share a common metaphysical core beneath their surface differences
Ultimate reality is a single divine ground from which all arises
Human beings have both outer (ego) and inner (divine spark) natures
The purpose of life is to realize one's ultimate identity with the divine ground
Mystical experience across traditions points to the same reality
Different religions are valid paths to the same summit
The inner, esoteric dimension of religion contains the universal truth
